cause.label: upstream of the UI: no access-tier enforcement exists on the serving path for these fields -- refined from the dispatch's own phrasing of cause (2)
cause.statement: The dispatch's cause (2) was framed as 'the atoms carry public-free, so the surface is correctly obeying policy.' The literal premise is not quite right and the corrected version is: there is currently NO ATOM, and therefore no accessPolicy value of any kind (public-free or otherwise), anywhere in the path that serves zoning, setbacks, utilityService, overlayDistricts, schoolDistrict, specialDistrict, pipeline, well, footprint, and boundary for this parcel. These fields are served by legacy-design-tools' per-rail 'ServeCutover' loaders (e.g. utilityServiceFactServeCutover.ts), which call hauska-engine's retrieval-api ONE-READER (GET /property-nodes/:id/record, parcel-record-reader.ts, built under P-152 2026-09-11) against the Factory's pre-atom parcel_record store. That reader dereferences an atom 'when a cell names one' (server.ts:381), but parcel-record-reader.ts:60 states plainly: 'Candidate field name for a future atom pointer on a cell (P-163 has not landed; no live cell carries one yet).' The live probe confirms this empirically: every rail served for node 48021:34841 came back with no atom attached. accessPolicy is real code in this codebase (server.ts's AccessPolicy union, enforced/surfaced on the unrelated /jurisdictions and /atoms/:did endpoints) but it is never consulted anywhere in the parcel_record/ONE-READER path -- not because the answer there is 'public-free', but because the question is never asked. The dispatch's own governing instruction for this exact situation applies without modification: 'a UI gate would leave every other consumer still serving the same body, the MCP catalog tools included' and 'the correct fix is to move it to a correctly-policied atom' -- which is P-163 (the atom-pointer cutover) landing plus an accessPolicy check being added to the ONE-READER, both outside this lane's scope.

evidence: Live A/B (this lane, 2026-09-14T17:34Z): GET https://smartsite.cloud/api/spine/property-atoms/48021:34841/facets, unauthenticated, with and without ?via=empressa -- HTTP 200 both times, response bodies identical (see _inbox/2026-09-14_173412_surface_probe.json, field identicalBodiesAfterDroppingVolatileClocks: true).

Source read of both p185 branches deployed today: legacy-design-tools feat/p185-promotekit-checkout-metadata (diff vs origin/main: pePaywallStripe.ts +24, new promotekitReferral.ts +65 lines, propertyExplorer.ts +19, two new test files -- 357 lines total, all Stripe Checkout Session metadata) and hauska-map feat/p185-promotekit-script-and-referral (diff vs origin/main: apps/property-explorer/index.html +13 -- one async <script src=https://cdn.promotekit.com/pk.js>, apps/property-explorer/src/lib/billingClient.ts +40, vercel.json CSP script-src widened by exactly one host). window.promotekit_referral is read in exactly one place in the client, billingClient.ts, at Stripe checkout time, and nowhere in the brief/facets fetch path. The ?via= param has no route to any server-side brief/facets code.
cause_1_p185_regression.basis: Two independent evidence lines (live behavioral A/B and source-diff read) agree.

cause_3_intentional_tier_width_pricing_r.evidence: No operator ruling, decision doc, or code comment found stating the free tier's brief width is a deliberate, current choice under change. The two fields that ARE gated (owner, CAD tax-assessed value) carry explicit, dated operator rulings (OPS-16 A-103 item 5, A-104, 2026-09-05: 'owner needs to be a part of unlock too... i just kept it out of solo as a way to graduate user through the tiers'). No equivalent ruling exists, anywhere searched, that says the other ten-plus fields (zoning, setbacks, utility service, overlay districts, school district, special district, pipeline, well, footprint, boundary, city limits) were deliberately left open. Their being open traces structurally to cause 2 (no gate mechanism exists on their serving path), not to a pricing decision about them specifically.

phase3_workingMechanism.mechanism: grantsOwnerCoGatedFields(userId, subscriptionTier, parcelNodeId) in legacy-design-tools/artifacts/api-server/src/lib/peEntitlement.ts -- true iff subscriptionTier is studio|team, OR the caller holds an active (unexpired) per-parcel Property Unlock.
phase3_workingMechanism.whereApplied: legacy-design-tools/artifacts/api-server/src/routes/brokerageNodeFacets.ts, the same route that serves every other field discussed here. Owner name/mailing: a typed 'studio-gated' refusal is returned and the owner-fact atom is not even queried for an ungranted caller (comment at line ~211: 'Anonymous, free, Solo, and identified-only brokerage sessions receive a typed studio-gated refusal ... and do not query atoms'). The four CAD tax-assessed dollar fields (marketValue, assessedValue, landValue, improvementValue): gateCadRollValuationOnFacets() in structuralFactToFacetsWire.ts runs AFTER the overlay merge and replaces each with a typed studio-gated refusal per field, using the SAME grantsOwnerCoGatedFields predicate -- never a second, independent check.
phase3_workingMechanism.whyItDoesNotGeneralize: This is bespoke, hand-written PE-tier business logic added for exactly these two field groups by name, on two dated operator rulings (2026-09-05). It does not read accessPolicy, is not a generic gate, and was never wired to any other field. The ten-plus fields the operator's screenshot showed open were never given an equivalent call because nobody has written one for them; they pass straight through the parcel_record/ONE-READER path described under cause 2, which has no gating concept of its own to extend.
phase3_workingMechanism.liveConfirmation: Same probe artifact: ownerFact_present true, ownerFact_ownerName 'ABSENT-OR-GATED'; cadRoll_marketValue and cadRoll_assessedValue both return {state:'refused', code:'studio-gated', reason:'County tax-assessed valuation ... is Studio or Team only ...'}. The gate is live, typed, and working exactly as the source describes.

proportion.verdict: PAID-TIER INTEGRITY, NOT A PRIVACY BREACH
proportion.basis: Every field this lane found open (zoning, setbacks, utility service/CCN detail, overlay district, school district, special district, pipeline, well, footprint, boundary, city limits) is Texas public land-use/GIS record data, not personally-identifying and not financial. The two fields that could plausibly be sensitive by the operator's own established distinction -- owner identity and CAD tax-assessed dollar figures -- ARE correctly gated and were live-confirmed gated for this exact parcel. The defect is that an anonymous visitor gets nearly the full commercial value of the 'More facts' brief for free, which is a monetization/tier-ladder integrity problem, not a data-exposure incident. Also note two fields on the brief's own field list, agValuation and maxImperviousCoverPct, are currently refused for THIS parcel for an unrelated reason -- 'not-cut-over': those two rails are only slated for Williamson/Travis counties today, not Bastrop -- so they should not be read as evidence of any gate, working or missing.

falsifier: Anonymous facets response for node 48021:34841 differs between a request carrying ?via=empressa and one that does not.
contradicted: The falsifier did not fire (bodies identical); hypothesis 1 (p185 regression) is eliminated by this lane's own test, contradicting the operator's stated intuition that today's PromoteKit deploy was the proximate cause. Also contradicted: the dispatch's own cause-2 wording ('atoms carry public-free') -- corrected in cause.statement above to 'no atom or accessPolicy check exists on this path yet', a materially different finding with a different fix (P-163 atom cutover + a new accessPolicy check in the ONE-READER, vs. relabeling an existing atom's policy value).
leave_behind: P-163 (atom-pointer cutover for parcel_record cells) has not landed; until it does, accessPolicy cannot be enforced on this serving path for any rail, not just the ones named in this dispatch. Whoever owns P-163 should know this AUTH-GATE finding names a second, independent reason to prioritize it beyond its original motivation.

The corrected phase-2 finding (no accessPolicy mechanism on the parcel_record/ONE-READER path, vs. atoms-carry-public-free) should be reflected wherever OPS-16 A-151/P-199 or its successor row is tracked, since the dispatch's own text currently states the less precise version.

missionPremise: OPS-16 A-151/P-199 (operator finding 2026-09-14): the Property Explorer brief serves fully unauthenticated except owner and CAD tax-assessed value, which are correctly Studio-gated; three mutually exclusive causes exist and picking the wrong one is worse than waiting, so naming the correct cause with eliminating evidence for the other two IS the deliverable unless phase 1 alone (an unambiguous p185 regression) settles it outright.
completionPredicate: A close naming exactly one of the three causes, with evidence eliminating the other two, plus the phase-3 answer for why owner/CAD-value are gated and nothing else is. This close does all three. Fix authority (conditional on cause 1) was never triggered, so no fix was made -- correctly, since making one would have been the exact 'field stripper at the surface' or unilateral atom-policy/tier change the dispatch explicitly forbids. status: closed reflects that the diagnosis (this row's actual deliverable) is complete, not that a fix landed.
scopeBasis: Read-mostly by dispatch design; no atom-policy change, no tier/pricing decision, no write to smartcity-os or smartcity-dashboards, no deploy -- all honored (zero commits, zero deploys, zero writes outside this lane's own _inbox/ and a local, uncommitted probe driver). The corrected cause (2) finding names P-163 and a future accessPolicy check as the actual fix, both explicitly out of this lane's scope per the dispatch, so they are reported in leave_behind rather than attempted.
